name: Andrey Melnichenko
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Andrey Melnichenko is the founder of fertilizer producer Eurochem and coal energy company SUEK.
The son of a Soviet physicist, Melnichenko dropped out of college when the Soviet Union fell in 1991 to start a chain of currency exchange booths.
Two years later, he founded MDM Bank, which became one of Russia's most successful private banks.
Melnichenko's companies, which employ more than 100,000, have invested some $23 billion into fertilizer and coal production over the past 15 years.
Melnichenko was sanctioned by the EU and UK in March 2022, and by  the US in August 2022; he called the sanctions "absurd and nonsensical" and is disputing them.
In 2022 Melnichenko's wife, Alexandra, became the beneficiary of a trust that holds stakes in Eurochem and SUEK.
forbes_facts: His yacht SY A, the world's largest sail-assisted yacht, has been frozen by Italian authorities.
Melnichenko has a collection of Impressionist art, including pieces by Claude Monet.

name: Folorunsho Alakija
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2014-2019); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Folorunsho Alakija is vice chair of Famfa Oil, a Nigerian oil exploration company with a stake in Agbami Oilfield, a prolific offshore asset.
Famfa Oil has partnered with Chevron.
Alakija's first company was a fashion label whose customers included the wife of former Nigerian president Ibrahim Babangida.
The Nigerian government awarded Alakija's company an oil prospecting license in 1993, which was later converted to an oil mining lease.
The Agbami field has been operating since 2008; Famfa Oil says it will likely operate through 2024.

name: Dean Solon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Dean Solon founded Shoals Technologies in 1996; it makes electrical gear for some of the biggest U.S. solar installations.
Solon, who stepped down as CEO to join the board, owns 40% of Shoals Technologies Group, which had its IPO in January 2021.
Solon got his start at age 8 carrying his dad's toolbox to repair air conditioners; by 16 he had his own customers.
He dropped out of Purdue University and was soon designing and manufacturing automotive parts.
He is the author of two dozen patents pertaining to solar gear.
forbes_facts: Since the 1970s Solon has visited Disney World at least twice a year. His favorite movie is Beauty And The Beast.
Shoals makes all its solar gear at four factories in Tennessee and Alabama; the company charges more than most competitors, but its products are seen as safer, more reliable and easier to install.

name: Cao Kanyu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Cao Kanyu is the president of Shanghai-listed memory chip giant CXMT, which raised in July 2026 $8.6 billion in one of the largest listings in Asia ever.
The company, also known as Changxin Memory Technologies, is the world's fourth largest producer of DRAM chips by market share, after Samsung, SK Hynix and Micro, according to Counterpoint Research.

Cao worked at a number of semiconductor companies in the U.S. and China - including the chip division of Dutch electronics giant Philips (now NXP Semiconductors) and GigaDevice - before joining CXMT in 2017.
The company's Chairman Zhu Yiming is also a billionaire.

name: Rodney Lewis
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2018); Hurun Global (2014-2016)
forbes_bio: Rodney Lewis grew up on the border in Laredo, Texas.
Lewis started Lewis Petro Properties in 1983 with one natural gas well.
He eventually acquired 500,000 acres in the Eagle Ford shale and became the fourth-biggest gas producer in Texas.
He owns America's biggest fleet of air-worthy World War II fighter planes, including a P-38 dug out of a Greenland glacier and restored.
In 2004 Lewis was the first U.S. oilman to sign a contract to drill for Pemex in Mexico.
forbes_facts: Lewis beat esophageal cancer a decade ago, but lost his salivary glands.
An avid collector of World War II-era fighter planes, Lewis is a board member of the National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C.
